 Business live Business Anthropic to float on the stock market today as it raises $81bn in record IPO – business live
 Rolling coverage of Anthropic’s IPO, and the latest economic and financial news
 LIVE  Updated  19m ago Graeme Wearden Thu 19 Nov 2026 04.36 EST First published on Thu 19 Nov 2026 03.04 EST Share Key events 25m ago Nationwide: AI helped us handle surge in current account openings 
 54m ago IMF chief: AI is exciting, though a bit scary 
 1h ago Anthropic shares 'indicated about 20% higher' in grey market 
 2h ago Introduction: Anthropic's record IPO ahead of today's stock market float 
 The logo of Anthropic is displayed on a smartphone screen . Photograph: VCG/Getty Images View image in fullscreen The logo of Anthropic is displayed on a smartphone screen . Photograph: VCG/Getty Images Graeme Wearden Thu 19 Nov 2026 04.36 EST First published on Thu 19 Nov 2026 03.04 EST Share From 2h ago 03.04 EST Introduction: Anthropic's record IPO ahead of today's stock market float
 Good morning, and welcome to our rolling coverage of the world’s biggest stock market listing, and other events across business, the financial markets and the world economy. 
 We’re going to see the biggest initial public offering in history today; Anthropic is floating on the US stock market, in what will be a major test for the market’s enthusiasm for the AI industry.
 Despite fears that AI may be a bubble, primed to pop, Anthropic – the frontier AI firm behind the Claude chatbot – has seen a surge of demand from investors looking to buy a stake.
 Last night, Anthropic announced it had raised a record-breaking sum from its IPO. In a sign of strong demand, the company increased the price at which its selling its shares to $83, up from a previous guide of $70-$78.
 That will raise $81.3bn (£61.8bn), exceeding the $75bn raised by Elon Musk’s SpaceX in June .
 If you include another $26bn raised through a private sale of shares to tech firms, Anthropic’s IPO has secured a record sum of $107.3bn, Sky News has calculated .
 Anthropic’s CEO Dario Amodei and his fellow co-founders are expected to ring the Nasdaq opening bell at 9.30am New York time (2.30pm in the UK).
 The company will then make its debut on the Nasdaq under the symbol “ANT”, although we may have to wait a little while before its shares start trading.
 Anthropic joins the market at a time when the Nvidia crisis has rattled investors. Tech stocks have dropped in recent weeks, pulling the Nasdaq Composite down by over 10% from its record high at the start of October.
 The IPO will value Anthropic at around $1.5tn (£1.1tn), placing it around 12th on the list of the world’s biggest companies .
 That’s despite the company being loss-making; in 2025 it posted an operating loss of over $8bn, as expenses (nearly $13bn) outpaced revenues ($4.6bn).
 Revenues have accelerated in 2026, though, but the company’s challenge is to a) maintain this, and b) turn it into profits.
 Garry White, chief investment commentator at wealth manager Raymond James, explains:
 double quotation mark “Anthropic’s IPO should be a clear litmus test of current market sentiment towards the AI investment boom. If the shares enjoy a strong post-listing rally, it would signal that markets remain convinced a handful of AI leaders can eventually generate profits large enough to justify today’s vast spending on talent, infrastructure and computing power.
 “Conversely, a weak reception or a sharp decline after flotation could suggest investors are becoming more selective, drawing a distinction between AI’s transformative potential and the commercial challenge of converting rapid revenue growth into sustainable earnings.
 The agenda
 10am GMT: A French government bond auction
 1.30pm GMT: US initial jobless claims data
 2.30pm GMT: Wall Street trading begins

 18m ago 04.24 EST Lauren Almeida Anthropic’s IPO could breathe life into London’s ailing high-end property market . 
 The share sale is likely to turn more than 4,000 of its staff into millionaires as their stock options vest. The company has 200 employees in the UK, and is planning a new London office capable of accommodating up to 800 people.
 Millionaire factory: Anthropic IPO set to fuel AI gold rush in London’s high-end property market Read more Share 25m ago 04.17 EST Nationwide: AI helped us handle surge in current account openings
 Kalyeena Makortoff Nationwide Building Society has become the latest lender to extol the virtues AI, saying it had been used “extensively” in onboarding customers amid a surge in current account openings for the first half of the year. 
 Bosses on Thursday said pre-tax profits surged 38% in the six months to September, compared to the same period last year, boosted in part by lower costs and higher revenues, including a 7% rise in net interest income (the difference between what it pays out to savers versus what it charges borrowers).
 Executives also said it had been a “record” first half of the year for current account openings, aided in part by AI. CEO Debbie Crosbie told reporters on an earnings call this morning:
 double quotation mark “AI is helping to guide our colleagues, serve them [customers] really well. So we’re doing AI a bit differently, we are always making sure humans are in the loop and..our colleagues to have a better understanding of how they best serve those needs.”
 When asked whether AI had fuelled the surge in current account openings, Crosbie said:
 double quotation mark “We use it extensively to assist the smoothing of that process.”
 However she was quick to point out that over 30% of accounts were still opened in person, in its branches (having made a pledge to keep all of its its 696 branches operating until at least 2030).
 While the building society has been slashing jobs in the wake of the Virgin Money takeover (including 275 job cuts announced last month) bosses said “savings are coming through from predominantly technology and third party expenditure” rather than job cuts.
 CFO Muir Mathieson said:
 double quotation mark “The reduction in cost doesn’t relate to people costs. In fact, our number of employees, and the people-related costs, has actually gone up.”
 That includes plans to hire 800 more staff as Nationwide launches its own-branded business bank accounts next year.
 Share 38m ago 04.05 EST The US stock market is set to open higher, which might help Anthropic make a smooth debut on the Nasdaq market. 
 The tech-focused Nasdaq index is on track to open 1.8% higher.
 Roger Lee , head of equity strategy at Cavendish , says:
 double quotation mark “Nvidia fell another 3% yesterday, perhaps not helped by Anthropic’s record IPO, which priced above the top of the range and valued Claude’s creator at $1.5tn. The record IPO was more than 7x covered and the shares are currently up c.20% pre-market, helping Nasdaq futures trade almost 2% higher.”
 Share 54m ago 03.48 EST IMF chief: AI is exciting, though a bit scary
 View image in fullscreen International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva attending the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen today Photograph: Wang Zhao/AFP/Getty Images IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva has been telling world leaders that AI has already been boosting growth in some countries. 
 Speaking at the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders ’ Meeting in Shenzhen, China, Georgieva said the transformative force of AI means we are in an “exciting, though a bit scary” time.
 Georgieva said AI was driving growth, although also fuelling inflation by driving up prices:
 double quotation mark This is the first year when AI had a material impact on global growth. It provided a counterbalance to the negative energy supply shock caused by the turbulence in the Middle East. And while the energy shock will eventually dissipate, AI is forever—making it the most significant factor for medium-term competitiveness, productivity, and growth.
 This year rapid AI-led acceleration in a dozen or so economies contributed to global growth of 3.1 percent, or 3.4 percent for APEC—better than feared but worse than needed.
 And she warns leaders that they face “a genuine urgency” to advance AI-related policies, saying:
 double quotation mark To put it simply: you snooze, you lose. Countries need digital infrastructure, labor markets and workers that are ready for AI, and risk mitigation—especially to control financial stability and cybersecurity risks.
 Share 1h ago 03.37 EST Anthropic shares 'indicated about 20% higher' in grey market
 Those who missed out on the Anthropic IPO (or didn’t receive as many shares as they hoped) will get the chance to buy them today once trading on the Nasdaq begins. 
 Bloomberg reports that Anthropic’s shares are indicated to open between 20% and 26% higher in grey market trading – based on a market run by IG , and one on the crypto platform Hyperliquid .
 They explain:
 double quotation mark Derivatives offered by online brokerage IG International pointed to a market value of $1.35 trillion Thursday morning in Hong Kong, implying a gain of more than 24% from the IPO price of $83. That valuation is based on the share classes sold in the deal, while the company’s fully diluted market value is roughly $1.5 trillion.
 Anthropic-tied perpetual futures — contracts that don’t expire — listed on the crypto platform Hyperliquid traded at around $101, a 20% premium from the pricing.
 Share 1h ago 03.32 EST UK investment platform Hargreaves Lansdown reports that 45,811 of its clients applied for Anthropic shares in the IPO. 
 The average application was for £6,661 worth of shares, and customers aged between 45 and 54 were the biggest buyer of Anthropic stock, they report.
 However, in a sign of the float’s popularity, Hargreaves Lansdown’s clients have only been allocated 33.6% of what they hoped to buy, which is “in line with other UK retail investors.”
 Share 1h ago 03.25 EST Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at investing and trading platform IG , reports that Anthropic has received “solid demand” from both retail and institutional investors.
 double quotation mark “The former in particular are clamouring to get on board, with demand from this corner more than 60% higher than the planned allocation.”
 Share 2h ago 03.09 EST Today will be a big payday for Anthropic’s seven co-founders, who are all becoming paper billionaires through the IPO. 
 Those co-founders are selling 23,648,646 shares, worth $1.96bn.
 Those shares are a small part of the 980,000,000 shares of Class A common stock which are being sold in the IPO.
 But it will raise the equivalent of $280m each for the co-founders: brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei, plus research engineer Tom Brown, former tech journalist turned public policy lead Jack Clark, Anthropic’s chief science officer Jared Kaplan, its chief architect Sam McCandlish, and its interpretability research lead Chris Olah. 
 These seven will all be worth around $20bn each , based on their full stakes in Anthropic.
